conditions: The target record is an issue (the action "set priority to Urgent" applies to an issue's priority field).
The issue's assignee is Priya Nair (exact person match).
The issue belongs to a milestone that is part of the Aurora project ("Aurora's milestone").
That milestone's due date is September 30 (presumably the nearest/contextually current occurrence, i.e. 2026, since no year is stated and today is 2026-09-26).
Either the milestone or the issue "hasn't started yet" (see ambiguity below) — i.e. some entity's status is unstarted.
Implicitly, exactly one issue satisfies all the above conditions (the request uses "the issue", assuming a unique match).

ambiguities.phrase: "milestone that's due September 30 and hasn't started yet"
readings: Both "due September 30" and "hasn't started yet" describe the milestone (the milestone itself has not started/has no progress yet) — the more grammatically natural reading, since "that's" attaches to the immediately preceding noun "milestone" and governs both conjoined predicates.

"Due September 30" describes the milestone, but "hasn't started yet" describes the issue's own workflow status (i.e. the issue is in an "Unstarted"/Todo state) — plausible because "unstarted" is a standard Linear issue-status category, and the issue is the entity being acted on.
September 30, 2026 — the nearest upcoming occurrence, given today is September 26, 2026.
September 30 of some other year, if the milestone's actual due date is in the past or a different year and that's simply the one meant.
